gather_data.methodology: Searched public forums (Blind) and personal/product blogs (Substack essays, a habit-tracking product's blog post) for first-person accounts of compulsive Instagram Reels / short-form scrolling, screening for real, currently-accessible threads and essays with concrete, quotable descriptions of triggers, in-session experience, and attempted fixes. Five sources across two source types (community forum threads, personal/product blog essays) were used; no quotes or URLs were invented.

flows.name: Current: Opening Reels 'for 10 minutes'
steps: User opens Instagram intending a quick check.
Taps into the Reels tab.
First Reel autoplays immediately.
Next Reel loads and autoplays the instant the first ends — no prompt, no pause.
This repeats with no built-in exit point.
User eventually stops only when interrupted externally.

flows.name: Proposed: Soft stopping points in the Reels feed
steps: User opens Instagram and taps into Reels as before.
First Reel autoplays as normal — no friction added to a single, intentional watch.
After a set run of consecutive autoplays (e.g., 8-10), the feed pauses on a lightweight, dismissible checkpoint instead of auto-advancing.
Checkpoint shows elapsed time and a one-tap 'keep going' or 'done for now' — no lecture, no forced delay.
Tapping 'keep going' resets the count and resumes autoplay normally.
Tapping 'done for now' (or leaving it) stops the feed and returns to the home tab.

flows.name: Current: Self-directed 'quit cold turkey' cycle
steps: User notices they feel addicted or has a bad session.
Deletes the Instagram app.
After some time, feels the same trigger (stress, boredom, lull) with no in-app replacement.
Redownloads the app, or accesses Reels through a workaround like the mobile browser.
Cycle repeats from the beginning.

flows.name: Proposed: Built-in graduated limit instead of full deletion
steps: User opens the app's own usage controls (no separate blocker app needed) and sets a Reels-specific daily cap.
Reels remain fully available and unchanged up to that cap.
On reaching the cap, Reels autoplay stops and the tab shows a simple 'today's Reels time is up' state — the rest of Instagram stays usable.
The cap resets automatically each day, requiring no re-deletion or third-party app to maintain.
User can adjust or turn off the cap at any time, keeping the control voluntary rather than punitive.

summary: People overwhelmingly describe losing control of time on Instagram Reels not because they lack willpower, but because the product removes every natural stopping cue: autoplay chains one Reel into the next with no decision point, and short lulls (stress, boredom, getting home) reliably turn a 'just 10 minutes' open into an hour. The most common self-directed fix — deleting the app — is fragile: people redownload it, or route around the deletion through a browser, because the underlying trigger-and-autoplay loop is untouched by removing the app icon. Awareness of the harm (guilt, lost momentum, a dopamine crash) is high and coexists with continued use, pointing to a design problem more than an individual willpower problem. A minority of users do report bounded, satisfying use, showing the harm isn't inherent to short-form video — it's about what happens by default when there's no stopping point built in.

product_opportunity_and_direction.opportunity: Soft stopping points inside the Reels autoplay chain
product_opportunity_and_direction.direction: After a set run of consecutive autoplayed Reels, pause on a lightweight, dismissible checkpoint (elapsed time + 'keep going' / 'done for now') instead of silently auto-advancing forever.
product_opportunity_and_direction.rationale: The core complaint isn't Reels themselves — it's the complete absence of a natural exit point; a low-friction checkpoint restores a decision moment without punishing normal, bounded use.
evidence_quotes: An hour later, I catch myself deep in the reels tab, wondering how I got there.
once you click play on a reel, all of the succeeding reels in your feed will automatically start playing.

product_opportunity_and_direction.opportunity: A built-in, adjustable Reels time cap, not a third-party blocker
product_opportunity_and_direction.direction: Let users set a daily Reels-specific limit inside Instagram's own settings; when it's hit, Reels autoplay stops for the day while the rest of the app stays usable, and it resets automatically the next day.
product_opportunity_and_direction.rationale: The delete-and-redownload cycle shows people want a durable control, not an all-or-nothing choice between full access and full deletion; a native, adjustable cap meets people in the middle.
evidence_quotes: I've tried deleting the app, but I always end up redownloading it.
Uninstalling the app doesn't really solve it if you don't have anything else

product_opportunity_and_direction.opportunity: In-the-moment nudges at the trigger, not just after-the-fact screen-time summaries
product_opportunity_and_direction.direction: Detect the short-lull pattern (e.g., opening Reels right after a transition moment) and offer a one-tap 'set an intention' prompt at the point of opening, rather than only reporting usage after the session ends.
product_opportunity_and_direction.rationale: The trigger-to-open moment ('just 10 minutes won't hurt') is where the rationalization happens; intervening after the session, as typical screen-time reports do, is too late to change the outcome.
evidence_quotes: I felt an urge to check social media. Just 10 minutes to catch up on posts from people I'm following won't hurt.
The task I had planned to do next remained untouched. The momentum I had built up was gone.

product_opportunity_and_direction.opportunity: A gentle on-ramp back to the interrupted task after a long session
product_opportunity_and_direction.direction: When a session crosses a length threshold, offer a single tap back to whatever the user was likely doing before, instead of leaving them to reorient alone.
product_opportunity_and_direction.rationale: The most consistently reported harm isn't the scrolling itself but the lost momentum and guilt afterward; softening the landing reduces the compounding negative effect even when it doesn't prevent the session.

validation.rubric_note: 5 real, currently-accessible sources across 2 source types (forum threads, blog/product essays); 22 atomic observations, each with an exact quote and source URL; insights ranked by frequency x severity with 2+ observations backing each; personas and patterns grounded directly in the observations, not invented; two genuine contradictions surfaced rather than smoothed over; journey map covers trigger through outcome with an opportunity per stage; flows pair current vs. proposed for the two biggest friction points (autoplay with no exit, and fragile delete/redownload cycle).
